To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the age of a firm is an important determinant of its borrowing cost, and the age dependence is mainly attributable to bank's learning about a firm's quality over time.

(i) the distribution of borrowing costs tends to become less right skewed over time, (ii) this shift of the distributions is mainly explained by the adaptation of borrowing costs as firms age, and (iii) the adaptation is not explained by the Diamond's reputation acquisition mechanism, but by bank's learning of the firm's true quality over time.
